context: ▶ Theorem 25. PprO2 ⊆ OP 2. P We note that the “non-promise” version of this inclusion, i.e. PO2 ⊆ OP 2 , was already established in [14]. However, this result does not carry over to the promise case. A similar phenomenon arises in the non-input-oblivious analogue of this question: while we know that P prSP PS2 ⊆ SP 2 [14], it still remains open whether P 2 ⊆ SP . 2 With this tool in hand, we can identify and show the strongest Karp–Lipton–style collapse that currently known. Namely, the collapse can be extended to PprOMA ⊆ PprMA , where prOMA is the input-oblivious version of prMA and therefore is contained in prMA. At the same time, Th. 25 allows us to show that PprOMA is also contained in OP 2 , thus making prOMA prMA P P smaller than both P and O2 ! Th. 25 also helps us to tighten the chain of containments between PprOMA and OP 2 using a newly defined OLP 2 class, an input-oblivious analogue of LP 2 (see Fig. 1).
